current_evidence: Neither the council page nor a search could be run: the shared WebFetch budget (400/hour, all agents) and the per-turn WebSearch budget were both exhausted, so the currency of the list is unverified. The page Grokbot read is the council's own 'planning application requirements' guidance with numbered Notes (up to at least Note 39), plus per-type checklist PDFs. It looks like the current web-based local list, but this was not confirmed.

issues.detail: List date and Date basis are blank ('Undated'). The page or the checklist PDFs should give an adoption, publication or 'last updated' date, but this could not be read this run.

Under Full planning, the labels for open space and contaminated land are swapped or misapplied. The 'Block plan / Site plan' row carries the loss-of-open-space/playing-field requirement, which is really the Open Space requirement. The 'Open space / play space assessment' row carries the land contamination trigger (homes, schools, nurseries, play areas; known or suspected contamination; YALPAG screening form for a single home).
issues.evidence: Open space row: 'nurseries or play areas playing fields or allotments ... the land is known to be contaminated ... complete the YALPAG Screening Form'; Block plan row: 'showing all open space affected by the proposal ... We will not normally approve the loss of open space...'.

issues.detail: Householder triggers from the householder checklist PDF are garbled table text. 'Foul Sewage' reads 'Foul drainage Note 21 Only for: assessment form', so the actual trigger ('a new or replacement non-mains sewerage system') has slipped into the start of the Heritage Statement row. 'Arboricultural' reads 'Tree report Note 39 Only where (as indicated on 'Trees and Hedges' section of the (arboricultural 1APP application form): statement)'.
issues.evidence: Heritage row: 'a new or replacement non-mains sewerage system Heritage statement Note 23 Only if: the red line boundary contains a listed building.'

issues.detail: Some Full planning triggers are fragments without thresholds. 'Flood Risk Assessment' begins mid-list ('- an FRA is always needed, whatever the flood zone') and loses the conditions it refers to. 'Heritage Statement' carries only what-to-include text. 'Travel Plan' carries only the generic 'You must show how your development could affect traffic...'. 'Viability Assessment' carries what-to-include text. The 'Statement of Community Involvement' row is really the wind-turbine pre-application consultation statement (2+ turbines or hub height over 15m), which is a narrower statutory requirement mislabelled as an SCI.
issues.evidence: FRA excerpt: '- an FRA is always needed, whatever the flood zone Check if your development is in a flood zone We only need an FRA if the development itself is in the flood zone.'

issues.detail: 'Landscaping scheme' is placed under 'Change of use - prior approval', but its own trigger limits it to major full and reserved matters applications and excludes change of use only.
issues.evidence: 'You must submit a landscaping scheme if you are applying for: full planning permission for a major development approval of reserved matters for a major development You do not normally need one for: a change of use only'.

issues.detail: Rows are missing from application types that the triggers name. Contaminated Land and Archaeological desk-based assessment appear only under Outline, although both triggers say 'full or outline planning permission'. Full planning has no Contaminated Land or Archaeology row. Listed building consent has no Heritage Statement row. Several Full rows (BNG, FRA, Heritage, Open space, Travel Plan, Viability, Block plan) are marked INFERRED.
issues.evidence: 'You must submit a desk-based assessment if you are applying for full or outline planning permission and...'; 'You must submit a land contamination assessment if you are applying for full or outline planning permission for...'.

issues.detail: Three local requirements captured only as process text have no app-type row. (1) Coastal Change Vulnerability Assessment: development in the coastal change area must consider erosion, flooding and sea defences. The tab_item is cut off at 'not block the En'. (2) Biomass boiler information request form, for proposals including a biomass boiler. (3) BNG Strategy, which the page calls 'a local requirement, see Note 14'. It sits only inside the inferred BNG row, with no mention of outline.
issues.evidence: tab_items: 'It must consider: the risk of coastal erosion and flooding existing sea defences...'; 'First, download the biomass boiler information request form (PDF)'; BNG row: 'a BNG Strategy - this is a local requirement, see Note 14'.

issues.detail: Most of the 13 tab_items are guidance or process text, not requirements: 'Why we ask for a scale bar...', 'Check your form meets the validation requirements We will check the form at validation.', three 'View an example of ... (PDF)' lines, 'you should not include sensitive personal information in any viability assessment', 'First, download the biomass boiler information request form', 'The validation team cannot decide this.', 'Check which ecology report you need (PDF)...', and 'Complete the nutrient budget Use the Lindisfarne nutrient neutrality calculator'. The fire statement item is a national requirement, not a local one.
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Submission rules' and 'Local forms / checklists' sections.

issues.detail: Only one type-specific checklist (Householder PDF) was read, though the page is organised by numbered Notes (up to at least Note 39) and per-type checklists. Grokbot captured about 25 distinct requirements, so some Notes are probably uncaptured. Advertisement consent, LDC, s73, discharge of conditions, permission in principle and the other '(none)' rows were not checked against any type-specific checklist.
issues.evidence: docs_read lists only planning-application-requirements and ValidationChecklistHouseholderPlanningPermission.pdf; 'Tree report Note 39'.

summary: The live source could not be fetched because the web budgets were exhausted, so the list's date and currency are unverified, and the workbook leaves it undated. Grokbot's own extracts show swapped open space and contamination triggers, garbled householder checklist rows, landscaping wrongly under change of use, and coastal change, biomass and BNG Strategy requirements captured only as process text.

withdrawn_issues.detail: This audit could not fetch the live source because the shared WebFetch and WebSearch budgets were exhausted. The issues above come from Grokbot's own extracted text, and the source contents and currency still need checking.
withdrawn_issues.evidence: Proxy: 'web-fetch budget for this session is exhausted: 400 per hour, shared by every agent'.
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The live page can be read now (fetched copy is 109k characters), and it supports the issues above. On currency, it says 'The checklist was republished on 1 April 2026 and will be reviewed again by 1 April 2027'.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. This was a note about what my helpers could not read, not a Grokbot error, so it is removed from the issue counts. The council stays on "Still to check by hand".
